analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/ssd-startup-expiry-not-corrupt.md, lines 1-7) and a small addition to docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (the date bump at line 3 and a new paragraph at head lines 88-91). No source code is in the supplied units. The docs say a complete checkpoint found past its TTL by the startup scan (`SSDHybridCheckpointStore.scanOnDisk`) is removed as expired and is no longer counted in `corrupt_drops_total`.

Relevant threat T-041 (SSD prefix cache, TB-007): the 30-minute sliding TTL and expiry deletion are mitigations. The changelog and docs say expired files are still removed at startup, so the documented retention bound is unchanged. The change affects only telemetry classification. I found no change to encryption, HMAC lookup tags, the TTL value, epoch handling or authorization.

Remaining integration question: the corresponding Swift change in SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift is not in this batch, so I could not verify that startup expiry still unlinks files. Also not verified: whether the expired-removal path still runs under `removalLock` and leaves the epoch unrotated. If the code diverges from the docs, expired ciphertext could persist past the TTL. Only the doc claim is reviewed here. A related secondary question is whether any monitoring treats `corrupt_drops_total` as a tamper signal, since expired files no longer appear there. That would be an operational-visibility consideration, not a vulnerability. No findings.
